topic: Memory Allocation Optimization with Boundary Tags
explanation: Boundary tags are data structures used in dynamic memory allocators to manage free and allocated blocks of memory.  They improve the efficiency of coalescing free blocks by storing essential information (like block size and allocation status) at the beginning and end of each block.  This facilitates faster memory allocation and deallocation, crucial for performance in systems dealing with frequent dynamic memory management.
syntax: Header: [Size, Allocated/Free Flag, ...payload...]  Footer: [Size, Allocated/Free Flag]

example_explanation: The example demonstrates an optimized boundary tag approach where footers are only needed for free blocks.  The allocated/free status of the previous block can sometimes be inferred from the current block's header. This reduces memory overhead compared to using a header and footer for every allocated block, significantly improving efficiency when dealing with many small memory allocations like in graph applications, as described in the provided text. The pseudo-code showcases the logic for coalescing free blocks, highlighting the role of the boundary tags (header and footer) in this process.   The optimization reduces memory overhead by eliminating footers in allocated blocks which improves space utilization in situations involving frequent small allocations.
